summary: Converts float3 spatial attributes such as P between Cartesian, spherical, cylindrical, screen-space, and normalized-device-coordinate systems, with configurable angle units and optional camera perspective context.

key_params.name: inputattrscope
key_params.note: Input float3 attribute or components to project

key_params.name: angunit
key_params.note: Degrees, radians, cycles, or normalized angle units

key_params.name: camera
key_params.note: Camera used for screen-space or NDC conversions

key_params.name: aspectcorrectuv
key_params.note: Respect aspect ratio for projection UVs

key_params.name: fov
key_params.note: Horizontal field of view for screen-space or NDC conversion

key_params.name: depthnear
key_params.note: Near clipping depth for NDC/screen conversion

key_params.name: depthfar
key_params.note: Far clipping depth for NDC/screen conversion

key_concepts: Projection POP converts float3 spatial attributes between Cartesian, spherical, cylindrical, screen-space, and normalized device coordinate systems.
From Coordinate System describes how to interpret the input attribute components; To Coordinate System describes the output representation.
Angle Units affect spherical and cylindrical angular components and can be degrees, radians, cycles, or normalized 0-1 values.
Screen Space and NDC conversions require camera/perspective context such as camera, aspect, FOV, and near/far depth.
Output Attribute Scope and attribute metadata let planners preserve the original P while writing converted coordinates to a separate attribute.
Projection changes coordinate representation, so downstream nodes should know whether an attribute is Cartesian geometry, spherical coordinates, or screen/NDC space.
common_gotchas: Screen Space and NDC conversions need camera and perspective settings; Cartesian-to-spherical conversions do not.
Normalized angle units are useful for texture mapping but differ from degrees, radians, and cycles.
Projection changes coordinate representation, not just scale; label attributes clearly when keeping both spaces.
